newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon government wins vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon government wins vote of confidence.

text.p: The government of Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri won a vote of confidence in parliament on Wednesday after a three-day debate despite attacks from some members who criticised its policy statement.
Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said 102 members of 121 present in the 128-seat house voted for the government, which was formed on November 7, while 19 voted against.
The government is the third in four years headed by Hariri, a 52-year-old billionaire tycoon spearheading Lebanon's reconstruction after the 1975-90 civil war.
During the debate some deputies said the policies of Hariri's two previous governments had impoverished the Lebanese.

Hours before the confidence motion, Lebanese troops began deploying in Beirut to stop planned anti-government demonstrations on Thursday during a general strike called by labour unions and opposition groups.
